summary: Specifies a Diameter mechanism for a server or proxy to redirect messages to an alternate domain without naming individual hosts, when S-NAPTR is not used. It updates Sections 6.13 and 6.14 of RFC 6733.

eli5.summary: A receptionist who says go to that other building, without saying which desk.

questions: what is diameter realm based redirection
what is result code 3011 in diameter
subtitle: How a Diameter server or proxy can point senders at a whole alternate realm instead of naming individual hosts.

tldr.problem: The Diameter base protocol's redirect agent can only hand back individual hosts, but an operator moving a service to another domain wants to point senders at the whole domain without listing its hosts.
tldr.mechanism: A Realm-based Redirect Server answers with a new result code, DIAMETER_REALM_REDIRECT_INDICATION (3011), plus one or more Redirect-Realm AVPs (620) naming the alternate realms. The proxy or client then finds a peer in that realm and resends the request.
tldr.outcome: Applications that opt in get realm-level redirection without S-NAPTR. The RFC updates the usage of two AVPs in RFC 6733 and is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 7075 is a Proposed Standard from November 2013 and has not been obsoleted or updated. It updates RFC 6733 regarding the Redirect-Host-Usage and Redirect-Max-Cache-Time AVPs.

sections.title: Why Redirect to a Realm
sections.content:
The Diameter base protocol, RFC 6733, has a basic redirection service provided by a redirect agent. The indication it returns gives the message sender one or more individual hosts to use as the destination.

Consider an operator that has offered a service but no longer wants to. It has arranged for an alternative domain to provide the service, and it keeps a redirect server to tell senders where to go. The original operator should not have to configure that server with a list of hosts in the other operator's domain. It should simply be able to redirect to the domain as a whole.
sections.eli5: If a shop moves to a new town, the old shop can put up a sign saying 'we are in the new town now'. It does not need to list every worker's name.

sections.title: Where the Mechanism Lives
sections.content:
With DNS-based dynamic peer discovery, realm redirection already works through S-NAPTR. The NAPTR record for the application in the original realm gets an empty FLAG field, and its REPLACEMENT field names the new realm for the next DNS lookup. The new realm can be arbitrary, because the RFC 6733 restriction that the replacement match the original query's domain does not apply here.

That discovery method is optional, though. For deployments that do not use S-NAPTR, support for realm-based redirection has to be specified as part of a Diameter application. Support for the application, found during the capabilities exchange, then implies support for the mechanism. A new application opts in by making the mechanism mandatory to implement and referencing this RFC normatively.

Because the behavior is application-specific, a plain redirect agent cannot do it. An application-aware Diameter server or proxy MUST do it. This node is called a Realm-based Redirect Server.

An application can say that redirection applies only to complete sessions starting with the initial message, or to every message. The difference matters only when redirection is first turned on. In the first case existing sessions are not disrupted. In the second, existing stateful sessions will be.
sections.eli5: Some towns use a phone book that can say 'this number moved'. For towns without one, each kind of shop has to agree ahead of time that it will handle moved-sign duty itself.

sections.title: How Nodes Behave
sections.content:
A node acting as a Realm-based Redirect Server MUST be configured with an application that incorporates the mechanism. The Local Action field in its routing table is set to LOCAL, an application-specific field says to perform realm-based redirection, and another application-specific field holds the realm identities to redirect to.

When such a server gets a request the mechanism applies to, it MUST reply with an answer that has the 'E' bit set and keeps the Hop-by-Hop Identifier. The answer MUST carry the Result-Code DIAMETER_REALM_REDIRECT_INDICATION, and each configured alternate realm goes in its own Redirect-Realm AVP. It MAY also include a copy of Redirect-Host-Usage, which SHOULD be REALM_AND_APPLICATION. If it does, Redirect-Max-Cache-Time MUST be included too. Redirection MAY be applied even if the request has a Destination-Host AVP, depending on operator policy.

A proxy that receives this answer MUST try to reroute the original request, and if it fails MUST forward the indication toward the client. To reroute, it:

  • selects one realm from the Redirect-Realm instances;
  • locates and establishes a route to a peer in that realm using the normal discovery procedures of RFC 6733;
  • updates its routing cache for the original realm and application, taking the two AVPs into account if present;
  • removes Destination-Host (if present) and Destination-Realm from the request, adds a new Destination-Realm with the selected realm, and forwards it;
  • if a step fails and other realms were listed, tries the next one.

A client MUST be ready to receive this result code, and SHOULD follow the same steps as a proxy to update its routing table and get service. Because the routing entry is cached, later requests for that application will go to the new realm until the entry expires, which matters if the redirect is meant to be temporary.
sections.eli5: The receptionist says 'try the other building'. The person asking picks one building from the list, walks there, and next time goes there first, unless the note says the advice runs out.

sections.title: The New AVP and Result Code
sections.content:
The Redirect-Realm AVP has code 620 and type DiameterIdentity. It names a realm to which a node that gets the redirect indication SHOULD route the original request.

The DIAMETER_REALM_REDIRECT_INDICATION protocol error code is 3011. It says the server decided that the request, within an application supporting realm-based redirection, could not be satisfied locally. The initiator SHOULD send the request directly to a peer within a realm identified in the response. When it is set, the Redirect-Realm AVP MUST be present.

The RFC also updates Sections 6.13 and 6.14 of RFC 6733. Redirect-Host-Usage and Redirect-Max-Cache-Time here apply to the peer discovered by a node acting on the redirect response, which extends their normal usage.
sections.eli5: There is one new error word meaning 'not here, go there' and one new label that holds the name of the place to go.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The general recommendations in Section 13 of RFC 6733 apply. Redirecting to a different realm implies a change in the business relationship between organizations. So before redirecting, the client or proxy MUST ensure that authorization checks have been performed at each connection along the path toward the new realm. Section 13 of RFC 6733 recommends TLS, DTLS or IPsec on each peer-to-peer connection, which allows those hop-by-hop checks.

A compromised node acting as a Realm-based Redirect Server could redirect many requests toward a victim domain and flood it. Secure peer connections and authorization checks make it possible for the victim to discover where the attack comes from, but the RFC states that this does not prevent such a DoS attack.

Since a proxy can change the Destination-Realm AVP, any cryptographic algorithm that uses that AVP as input would be broken by this redirection. Application specifications relying on such algorithms SHOULD NOT incorporate realm-based redirection.
sections.eli5: Sending people to another company's door needs that company's agreement. A fake receptionist could send a crowd to someone's door, so the doors must check who is knocking.

sections.title: IANA Allocations
sections.content: IANA allocated the AVP code 620 for Redirect-Realm in the "AVP Codes" registry under "Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) Parameters". It also allocated the Result-Code value 3011 for DIAMETER_REALM_REDIRECT_INDICATION in the "Result-Code AVP Values (code 268) - Protocol Errors" registry in the same group.
sections.eli5: The number registry keeper wrote down the new label's number and the new error word's number so nobody else uses them.
